short_description: Resident scavenger cell of the heart with a rare second job: an elongated, spindled macrophage wedged between cardiomyocytes that not only clears debris but couples to the muscle cells through connexin-43 gap junctions and helps carry the electrical impulse through the atrioventricular node.
do_not_draw: a free-floating round blood monocyte among red blood cells
a giant multinucleate cell / foreign-body giant cell — exactly one nucleus
the macrophage without a cardiomyocyte contact and without visible connexin-43 plaques
bacteria being eaten as the main event
cell wall, nucleoid, plasmids, chloroplasts, large central vacuole
a full intercalated disc as the macrophage's junction
a confluent sheet of immune cells

colour_legend.nucleus: muted blue-violet with a paler nucleolus
colour_legend.phagosome: pale vesicle with grey engulfed debris fragments inside
colour_legend.mitochondrion: soft warm ochre-brown with faint cristae
colour_legend.cardiomyocyte: dusty rose / muted salmon with paler cross-striations
colour_legend.connexin43_plaque: distinct bright turquoise beads bridging the two membranes
colour_legend.background: neutral dark charcoal (textbook, 3d) / warm aged paper (watercolor)

reference.attribution: Louisa Howard, Dartmouth Electron Microscope Facility, via Wikimedia Commons
reference.caveat: Generic tissue-resident (pulmonary alveolar) macrophage, NOT a cardiac macrophage; no freely-licensed micrograph of a cardiac resident macrophage or of macrophage–myocyte connexin-43 coupling could be found.
